newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-UNITED'S LATEST FIXTURE APPEAL REJECTED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-UNITED'S LATEST FIXTURE APPEAL REJECTED.

text.p: Manchester United had their latest appeal for an extension to the league season rejected by the English Football Association (F.A.) on Friday.
United were seeking permission to play their vital match against Newcastle after the official end of the season on May 11.
They currently face a punishing schedule of four key games in nine days as they bid to retain their league title as well as win the European Cup.

Their original appeal, which sparked a public row between United manager Alex Ferguson and his opposite numbers at title rivals Liverpool and Arsenal, was rejected by the premier league earlier this month.
United then wrote to the F.A. asking them to over-rule the league, but on Friday F.A. chief executive Graham Kelly said that was impossible.
"Our rules do not allow us to over-rule the decision of the premier league board on matters such as fixtures and the date when the season ends," he told BBC Radio.
"We have told Manchester United that. They have written and we have replied."
The Association's response came a day before leaders United take on second-placed Liverpool at Anfield in a potential championship decider.
Liverpool will go a point clear of United if they win on Saturday although Ferguson's side would still have a match in hand.
The rivalry between United and Liverpool, already the most ferocious in English soccer, has intensified in the past fortnight as the row over fixture congestion has rumbled on.
"If Manchester United were to be given an extra week to complete their fixtures it would be totally out of order," Liverpool boss Roy Evans said.
"No club should gain an advantage. Like them, we have to play four games inside nine days and it seems like a funny time to start changing the rules."
Ferguson, fuelling a confrontation his club started, said he believed Liverpool and third-placed Arsenal had conspired to deny United the extra time they requested.

Saturday's match will almost certainly be the last of the season for Liverpool's England striker Robbie Fowler, who was sent off in their midweek 1-1 draw at neighbours Everton and faces a three match suspension.
Fowler, Liverpool's top scorer this season, looks set to miss his side's final league matches against Tottenham, Wimbledon and Sheffield Wednesday.
His absence will allow striker Stan Collymore to re-establish himself in the first team at a crucial stage of the season.
United face fitness tests to Danish goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel, defenders Denis Irwin and David May and Welsh winger Ryan Giggs.
Ferguson has said he hopes at least two of them will be fit to face Liverpool but his main priority is still Wednesday's European Cup semifinal second leg tie against Borussia Dortmund.
While the northern giants battle it out at Anfield, Arsenal, the only other side in a position to win the championship, entertain Blackburn.
Arsenal are the premier league's in-form side having won five of their last six matches, but with fixtures running out, they desperately need another victory on Saturday to stay in the running.
At the bottom of the table, Middlesbrough return home from an exhausting week of domestic cup ties to face neighbours Sunderland in a crucial relegation battle.
